title: Bundle analysis and code splitting
description: Learn about Bundle analysis and code splitting. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Bundle analysis and code splitting are essential techniques for optimizing JavaScript delivery. Bundle analysis helps you understand what's in your bundles and identify optimization opportunities, while code splitting breaks your application into smaller chunks that can be loaded on demand.
Bundle analysis involves examining the composition, size, and dependencies of your JavaScript bundles. This helps identify large dependencies, duplicate code, and opportunities for optimization.

data.text: Code splitting divides your JavaScript into smaller bundles that can be loaded on demand. This reduces the initial JavaScript payload and improves load times, especially for large applications.

data.text: Separate vendor dependencies from application code. This allows vendor code to be cached independently and reduces the impact of application changes on cache invalidation.

data.title: Over-Splitting Risks
data.text: Don't over-split your bundles. Too many small chunks increase HTTP overhead and can hurt performance. Aim for chunks between 20KB-200KB.
Set up continuous monitoring of bundle sizes in your CI/CD pipeline to catch size regressions before they reach production.

data.title: Bundle Size CI Check
data.content: Enforce bundle size limits in CI/CD.
data.code:
// .github/workflows/bundle-size.yml
name: Bundle Size Check
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  bundle-size:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v2
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: andresz1/size-limit-action@v1
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          skip_step: install
          build_script: npm run build

// package.json
"size-limit": [
  {
    "path": "dist/*.js",
    "limit": "200 KB"
  },
  {
    "path": "dist/vendors*.js",
    "limit": "150 KB"
  }
]

points: Bundle analysis identifies large dependencies and optimization opportunities
Code splitting reduces initial JavaScript payload by loading code on demand
Use dynamic imports and React.lazy() for component-level splitting
Implement route-based splitting for optimal initial load performance
Separate vendor code from application code for better caching
Monitor bundle sizes in CI/CD to prevent regressions
Balance splitting benefits against HTTP overhead costs
data.takeaway: Bundle analysis and code splitting are fundamental techniques for optimizing JavaScript delivery and improving application load performance.
